note: Per-batch VRAM budget and throughput on one W7800 48GB. Each batch value is its own engine restart; slots and expert-cache figures come from the engine's own startup lines.
method: tools/serve_load.py --max-tokens 128 --rounds 3, requests marked fresh (conversation cache cannot help)

throughput.note: 0 tokens in 21.6 s: single request already starved

tier_state.note: files N blobs is the engine's own count of expert-file reads; it stays 0 at every batch value, so the cliff is not SSD reading.

conclusion: Each slot costs about 1 GiB of VRAM and displaces about 404 expert-cache slots. Up to 3 the batch pays (3 clients: 93.3 vs 84.2 tok/s, +10.8%); from 4 it collapses to 0.1 tok/s although the server reports no errors, because hot experts no longer fit in VRAM and must be fetched from the RAM tier over PCIe every step. Not an SSD problem: resident RAM grows with the batch and the engine reads 0 blobs from files.
production_choice: batch 3, parallel 3, max_queue 3 (admission limit 6): 9 simultaneous requests gave 6 x 200 and 3 x 429, c=3 95.3 tok/s (+13.2% over batch 2).
